name: bm-r5-explicit-3d-confinement
title: Explicit 3D cell confinement
claim: A 3D monolayer with volume and surface energies runs and yields per-cell heights; the no-membrane, elastic-membrane and relaxing-membrane controls are the next step.
question: Do growing 3D epithelial cells become taller when the basement membrane relaxes slowly?
hypothesis: In a Tyssue 3D monolayer with apical/lateral/basal energies and cell-volume targets, cells confined by a slowly-relaxing BM grow taller (smaller basal area, larger height) than under elastic or absent BM, reproducing the core morphology ordering of the paper.
objective: Build a Tyssue 3D monolayer with apical/lateral/basal energies and cell-volume targets; run no-BM, elastic-BM and relaxing-BM controls; measure height, basal/apical area, their distributions and growth trajectories against the paper's morphology ordering.
description:
The explicit 3D reproduction (plan section 3, 3D monolayer level). Real cell heights and
basal expansion emerge from apical/basal/lateral surface energies and volume constraints
rather than an inferred prism relation. The no-BM / elastic-BM / relaxing-BM controls
isolate the BM-relaxation contribution to cell height. Establishing the cell-height and area
response here gates P2 and is the substrate for the closed lumenoid (E3).

expected_behavior.name: taller-under-slow-relaxation
expected_behavior.observable: cell height / basal area distribution vs BM relaxation
expected_behavior.rationale: Reproducing the morphology ordering (taller cells under slow BM relaxation) across the three BM controls is the P2 success criterion.

baseline.name: bm-r5-explicit-3d-confinement
baseline.note: A 3D epithelial monolayer of 206 cells with apical, basal, and lateral surfaces and per-cell volume targets, so cell height and basal area emerge directly instead of from a thin-prism approximation. Cases with no membrane, an elastic membrane, and a relaxing membrane isolate what the membrane's relaxation contributes to cell height.
